correctness.rationale: The polar of the symmetric edge polytope in the zero-sum space is exactly the graph Lipschitz polytope. The published complete-multipartite facet classification gives every polar vertex after subtracting its mean. Type-(i) squared norms are q-(2t-q)^2/N and are maximized on a largest part with the most balanced sign split; type-(ii) squared norms are t(N-t)/N and are maximized at a balanced binary level size. Explicit feasible labelings attain both candidate bounds, so the polar circumradius and hence the inradius are exact. The spread identity follows from ||f-mean(f)||^2=N Var(f).

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are the explicit multipartite family singled out in the source's facet theory and include the classical complete and complete-bipartite cases. The result identifies a sharp structural phase competition between a largest-part extremizer and a globally balanced cut, simultaneously computing a canonical Euclidean polytope radius and a classical Lipschitz-variance graph invariant. The equality cases identify which published facet type actually controls the metric. This is a family-wide structural theorem rather than a finite table or routine single-parameter increment.
